The Ultimate Highland Park Food Crawl: 8 Must-Try Ethnic Eateries in Des Moines

Nestled in Des Moines' historic Highland Park neighborhood, a vibrant collection of family-owned ethnic restaurants and international markets offers food lovers an incredible culinary journey around the world. This diverse dining district, centered along 6th Avenue just north of downtown, has become one of Central Iowa's most exciting food destinations.

A Global Food Adventure in Historic Highland Park

Highland Park's rich immigrant history dates back to the early 1900s when European settlers first made this neighborhood their home. Today, that cultural diversity lives on through an eclectic mix of eateries representing cuisines from Latin America, Asia, Africa, and beyond.

8 Must-Visit International Restaurants

1. Mi Patria - Ecuadorian Excellence

Start your food crawl at this beloved Ecuadorian restaurant known for their incredible empanadas and fresh seafood dishes. Don't miss their signature hornado - slow-roasted pork served with llapingachos (cheese-stuffed potato cakes).

  • Location: 1410 6th Ave
  • Must-try dish: Pescado Encocado (Fish in Coconut Sauce)
  • Best time to visit: Weekend lunch for the full experience

Planning Your Highland Park Food Crawl

Best Times to Visit

Weekend afternoons are ideal for this food adventure, though be aware that some restaurants close between lunch and dinner service. During Des Moines' warmer months (May-September), you'll find additional outdoor seating options.

[Additional planning details...]

Local Tips and Insider Knowledge

  • Many restaurants are family-owned and close for major holidays
  • Street parking is usually available along 6th Avenue
  • Consider timing your visit during the World Food & Music Festival in September
